why: This checker guards a downgrade that nothing else refuses. kagent admits a ModelConfig with a spec.tls block beside an http:// baseUrl: nothing fails, the block is inert, the seam is plaintext, and the manifest reads as configured. It also admits an https:// baseUrl with no tls block, which fails every call as a generic connection error far from its cause. So the checker has to fail in every way it could stop noticing either half — the scheme test, the missing-authority test, the disableVerify test, the two identity tests, the recogniser that finds no seam URLs or every URL, an empty run reported as clean, and a verdict computed and dropped. The FIXTURES are mutated too: a self-test whose broken cases stop being broken passes while checking nothing, and that is the failure this harness cannot otherwise see.

mutations.name: a plaintext seam URL is no longer a problem
mutations.breaks: The half that matters most. Every manifest could point at the seam over http, carry a tls block that is never used, and read exactly like one that is verified.

mutations.name: an https seam with no authority passes
mutations.breaks: The other half. The agent verifies against the system trust store, which has never heard of the plane, and every call fails with a message that names nothing.
